messages:
maria: running nsys on the dedicated pool and it crashes during CUPTI init. the qdrep is produced but the CUDA kernel events are missing, so our kernel-timeline looks empty. anyone hit this?

samir: what versions? nsys + driver + distro?

maria: nsys 2024.1, CUDA toolkit libs from /usr/local/cuda-12.2, driver 535.54, ubuntu 22.04. stack:
```
nsys: CUPTI failed to initialize: CUPTI_ERROR_INTERNAL (0x00000006)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what(): CUPTI init failed
#0  0x7f9b...
```

evan: yep similar to a head-scratcher I saw earlier. nsys 2024.x bundles expect a matching libcupti ABI that wasn't guaranteed with driver 535 patches. sometimes it silently falls back and you lose kernel events, other times it segfaults.

ryan: we observed the perf regression on the runtime after trying to instrument batching hotpaths. timeline lacked the fused kernels and tracing showed extra memcpy stalls, ~12-18% tail-latency increase. I'm guessing the profiler changed kernel selection heuristics because CUPTI couldn't interrogate kernels.

samir: quick checklist: (1) confirm system libcupti used by nsys (LD_LIBRARY_PATH), (2) check for multiple libcupti installs, (3) try older nsys or driver combo. can you paste `ldd $(which nsys) | grep cupti` and `ls -l /usr/local/cuda*/extras/CUPTI/lib64/`?

maria: pasted outputs:
```
$ ldd $(which nsys) | grep cupti
libcupti.so.14 => /usr/local/cuda-12.2/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so.14 (0x7f9b...)
$ ls -l /usr/local/cuda-12.2/extras/CUPTI/lib64/
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 12345678 Jan  5 12:34 libcupti.so.14
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 2345678  Feb 10 09:11 libcupti.so.14.0.0
```

maria: also saw in syslog: `CUPTI: failed to open driver (Permission denied)` but I was running as root in the container. messed with seccomp?

evan: containers + seccomp and newer drivers are a common footgun. if the host kernel has a restrictive seccomp profile, open/attach to driver debug nodes can be blocked. also check nvidia-container-cli and /dev/nvidia* permissions.

samir: try two quick repros: (A) run nsys on host (not container) to confirm it's container/seccomp related, (B) run nsys with CUPTI disabled: `nsys profile --sample=none --trace=nvtx ./bin/serve` (this avoids CUPTI but loses kernel-level metrics).

maria: did (A) host run — same error. so not container. did (B) and it runs but timeline lacks kernel durations (we get NVTX regions only).

ryan: workaround that helped me: downgrade to nsys 2023.5 or pin driver to 525.x where libcupti ABI matched. also filing an issue with NVIDIA for 535.x + nsys 2024 mismatch.

evan: I also found a fragile workaround: preload the matching cupti from CUDA toolkit that nsys was built against. e.g.
```
LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so.14 nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx ./bin/serve
```
works sometimes but is dangerous in prod.

maria: tried LD_PRELOAD with cuda-12.1 cupti, it got past init and captured kernels, timeline now shows the missing fused kernel and memcpy hotspots. perf delta dropped back to expected.

ops-bot: perf-ci job #4827: reproduced locally and failed. created ticket PERF-712 to track pinned nsys/tooling matrix in CI.

samir: action items:
- ops to test driver rollback to 525 on staging and verify profiling pass (ops: @evan)
- pin nsys in our perf CI to 2023.5 until NVIDIA confirms compatibility (samir)
- add a startup check in our profiling helper that asserts libcupti ABI/version and warns if mismatch (maria/ryan)
- file a case with NVIDIA and attach qdrep + nsys stdout/stderr (maria)

evan: +1. I'll roll a staging node with driver 525 tomorrow morning, leave a note in the infra runbook about the LD_PRELOAD hack as emergency-only.

maria: thanks. I'll attach the qdrep and logs to PERF-712 and link the NVIDIA case once created. if anyone needs the failing binary/trace repro, ping me. :thumbsup:
